get_order_history.description: Get a batch of the Amazon Order history for a given time period, with a cursor to fetch the next batch.

parameters.year: The year for which to get history. Ignored if `time_filter` or `cursor` is provided. Defaults to the current year if neither `year` nor `time_filter` is specified.
parameters.time_filter: The time filter to use. Supported values are `"last30"` (last 30 days), `"months-3"` (past 3 months), or `"year-YYYY"` (specific year). If provided, this takes precedence over the `year` parameter.
parameters.order_filter: The order type filter to use, e.g. `"digital-orders"` for Kindle and other digital purchases, which the default history doesn't include. If provided, appended alongside the time filter.
parameters.family_member_id: The ID of an Amazon Household member whose Orders to get, such as a linked Teen account, from `get_family_members`.
parameters.start_index: The index of the Order from which to start fetching in the history. Ignored if `cursor` is provided.
parameters.full_details: Get the full details for each Order in the batch. This will execute an additional request per Order.
parameters.limit: Stop fetching history pages once at least this many Orders are collected. Whole pages are fetched, so the batch can hold up to a page more than `limit`. `None` fetches every page.
parameters.cursor: The `cursor` of the previous batch, to fetch the next one. The filters it was fetched with carry over.

output_schema.description: The batch of Orders, and the cursor for the next one.

items.description: An Amazon Order. If desired fields are populated as `None`, ensure `full_details` is `True` when retrieving the Order (for instance, with `get_order_history`), since by default it is `False` (enabling slows down querying).

full_details.description: If the Orders full details were populated from its details page.

index.description: Where the Order appeared in the history when it was queried. This will inevitably change (e.g. when a new Order is placed, all indexes will then be off by one), but is still captured as it may be applicable in various use-cases. Populated when the Order was fetched through `get_order_history` (use `start_index` to correlate), or when the `clone` has its `index` set.

cancelled.description: `True` if the Order was cancelled. When `True`, fields like `grand_total` and the totals on the details page may be `None` because Amazon stops rendering them.

is_whole_foods.description: `True` if this is a Whole Foods Market purchase (an in-store/FOPO purchase or a Whole Foods receipt order). Unlike other unsupported order types, these expose a `grand_total` and (often) an `item_count` on the history page, so those fields are populated.

get_tracking.description: Get the carrier and tracking number of a Shipment from its package tracking page.

parameters.order_id: The Amazon Order ID of the Shipment.
parameters.shipment_id: The Shipment's `shipment_id`. Amazon stops showing the tracking link it comes from on older Orders.

output_schema.description: The requested Tracking. Its fields are `None` when the page only shows the delivery milestones (no carrier tracking).

carrier.description: The carrier name, e.g. `UPS`, or `Amazon` for Amazon's own delivery network.

tracking_number.description: The carrier's tracking number, e.g. `1Z999AA10123456784` or `TBA000000000000`. Always a `str`, since many (e.g. USPS) are all digits and may have leading zeros.

search_orders.description: Search every year of the Order history for Orders by product title, Order number, address, or recipient, as the search box on Your Orders does, getting each matching Item with its Order's number and date.

parameters.query: What to search for: words from a product title, an Order number, or a name or address an Order was sent to.
parameters.limit: Stop fetching result pages once at least this many results are collected. Whole pages are fetched, so the batch can hold up to a page more than `limit`. `None` fetches every page.
parameters.cursor: The `cursor` of the previous batch, to fetch the next one.

output_schema.description: The OrderSearchResults, one per matching Item, or an empty list if nothing matched.

items.description: An Item of an Order that matched an Order search. The Order search page lists each matching Item, with its Order's number and date, from every year of the Order history. The Order itself is fetched by `order_number` with `get_order`.

order_details_link.description: The Order details link. `None` if the result has none.

order_number.description: The number of the Order the Item is in, from `order_details_link`.

order_placed_date.description: The date the Order was placed.

item.description: The matching Item, built with the config's `item_class`. The search page shows its title, link, image, and quantity (only when more than one was ordered), not its price or Seller.

link.description: The Item link. `None` for items without an Amazon detail page (e.g. ASINLESS Whole Foods Market line items).

asin.description: The product ASIN, derived from `link`; `None` when the link is not a product page.

quantity.description: The Item quantity. `None` when the page shows none, and for items sold by weight (e.g. Whole Foods), which have no whole-unit count.

items.description: The results in this batch.

cursor.description: Pass this back as `cursor` to the same call to fetch the next batch. A JSON-safe `dict` to keep as it is, not to build or change. `None` when there are no more results.

has_more.description: `True` if there are more results to fetch with `cursor`.

get_invoice_pdfs.description: Get the invoice PDFs (invoices and credit notes) of a given Amazon Order ID from its invoice list.

parameters.order_id: The Amazon Order ID to lookup.

output_schema.description: The Order's InvoicePdfs, empty if Amazon lists none.

items.description: An invoice PDF of an Amazon `Order`, such as an invoice or a credit note, parsed from the Order's invoice list. See `get_invoice_pdfs`, and `download_invoice_pdf` for the document itself.

order_number.description: The Order number the document belongs to.

name.description: The document's name, as Amazon lists it, e.g. `Invoice`, `Invoice 2`, or `Credit note`.

link.description: The link to download the document. Amazon generates a new one on each request, so don't store it, get the Order's invoices again instead.

is_credit_note.description: `True` if the document is a credit note (a refund) rather than an invoice.

items.description: The Order's InvoicePdfs, empty if Amazon lists none.

get_transactions.description: Get a batch of Amazon Transaction history for a given number of days, or for a single Order, with a cursor to fetch the next batch.

parameters.days: The number of days worth of Transactions to get. Ignored when `order_id` or `cursor` is given.
parameters.order_id: If given, only Transactions for this Amazon Order ID are returned, as in `get_transactions`. Ignored when `cursor` is given.
parameters.limit: Stop fetching Transaction pages once at least this many Transactions are collected. Whole pages are fetched, so the batch can hold up to a page more than `limit`. `None` fetches every page.
parameters.cursor: The `cursor` of the previous batch, to fetch the next one. The `days` window or `order_id` it was fetched with carries over.

output_schema.description: The batch of Transactions, and the cursor for the next one.

items.description: An Amazon Transaction.

payment_method_last_4.description: The Transaction payment method's last digits, parsed from `payment_method`. `None` if no masked digits.

grand_total.description: The Transaction grand total, negative for a charge and positive for a refund.

is_refund.description: The Transaction was a refund or not.

order_number.description: The Transaction Order number, or `None` when the row carries no Order number.

seller.description: The Transaction seller name, or `None` when the row carries none.

items.description: The results in this batch.

cursor.description: Pass this back as `cursor` to the same call to fetch the next batch. A JSON-safe `dict` to keep as it is, not to build or change. `None` when there are no more results.

has_more.description: `True` if there are more results to fetch with `cursor`.

get_gift_card_activity.description: Get Amazon Gift Card activity for a given number of days.

parameters.days: The number of days worth of Gift Card activity to get.

output_schema.description: A list of the requested GiftCardActivity, newest first.

items.description: An entry in the Amazon Gift Card activity ledger, such as a Gift Card applied to an Order, a claim code redemption, a Reload, or a refund.

amount.description: The GiftCardActivity amount, negative when the balance was debited and positive when it was credited.

is_credit.description: The GiftCardActivity credited the balance or not.

closing_balance.description: The Gift Card balance after this GiftCardActivity.

order_number.description: The Order number the GiftCardActivity references, or `None` when the row links no Order.

order_details_link.description: The Order details link, or `None` when the row links no Order.

items.description: A list of the requested GiftCardActivity, newest first.

get_prime_payments.description: Get every charge in the Prime membership payment history.

output_schema.description: A list of the PrimePayments, newest first.

items.description: A charge in the Prime membership payment history: the membership fee Amazon billed on a sign-up or renewal date. Each charge is a digital Order (a `D01-` ID) that neither the Order history nor the Digital Orders tab lists, so this entity is the index to it. The Order itself is fetched by `order_number` with `get_order`, which renders the standard Order details layout for these IDs.

payment_date.description: The date the membership fee was charged, not the start of the membership period it covers.

order_number.description: The digital Order number (`D01-…`) of the charge.

order_details_link.description: The Order details link. `None` when `order_number` is `None`.

receipt_link.description: The "View Receipt" link, the digital Order summary's print view. `None` when the card has none.

items.description: A list of the PrimePayments, newest first.

get_family_members.description: Get the members of the Amazon Household whose Orders this account can view, such as linked Teen accounts, from the Order history's member filter.

output_schema.description: The FamilyMembers, or an empty list if the account has none.

items.description: A member of the Amazon Household whose Orders the account can view, such as a linked Teen account. Pass its `id` as `family_member_id` to `get_order_history` to get their Orders.
The FamilyMembers, or an empty list if the account has none.
